company.name: TotalEnergies SE
company.description: TotalEnergies SE, an integrated energy company, produces and markets oil and biofuels, natural gas, biogas and low-carbon hydrogen, renewables, and electricity in France, the United States, Europe, Africa, and internationally. It operates through Exploration & Production, Integrated LNG, Integrated Power, Refining & Chemicals, and Marketing & Services segments. The Exploration & Production segment engages in the activities of exploration and production of oil and natural gas, as well as carbon storage. The Integrated LNG segment is involved in the upstream and midstream LNG activities, as well as biogas and synthetic methane activities, as well as gas trading. The Integrated Power segment engages in the generation, storage, electricity trading, and B2B-B2C distribution of gas and electricity. The Refining & Chemicals segment is involved in the industrial hub activities comprising the activities of refining, petrochemicals and specialty chemicals. This segment also includes the activities of oil supply, trading and marine shipping, as well as hydrogen activities. The Marketing & Services segment engages in the marketing activities in the field of petroleum products, as well as corresponding supply and logistics activities. The company was formerly known as TOTAL SE and changed its name to TotalEnergies SE in June 2021. TotalEnergies SE was incorporated in 1924 and is headquartered in Courbevoie, France.

events.text: TotalEnergies (ENXTPA:TTE): Net Margin Slips, Undervaluation Focuses Debate on Dividend Risks
events.context:
TotalEnergies (ENXTPA:TTE): Net Margin Slips, Undervaluation Focuses Debate on Dividend Risks
TotalEnergies (ENXTPA:TTE) reported earnings growth forecasts of 3.54% per year and revenue is projected to expand at 3.4% per year, both trailing behind the broader French market’s expected 12.3% earnings and 5.5% revenue growth. The company’s net profit margin slipped to 7.7% from 8.3% the prior year, though it averaged 21.5% annual earnings growth over the last five years, returning to profitability in that span. Investors are watching a company trading at a significant discount to both peers and estimated fair value, underpinned by a strong track record and a robust, if slower, growth outlook. Dividend sustainability is the key risk to monitor.

French energy giant TotalEnergies resumes Mozambique $20 billion project as insurgency slows
HARARE, Zimbabwe (AP) — French energy giant TotalEnergies announced on Thursday the resumption of its $20 billion gas project in northern Mozambique that was halted in 2021 because of an insurgency in the area that killed thousands and displaced more than 1 million people.

events.text: TotalEnergies halves buybacks as low oil, gas prices weigh on profits
events.context:
TotalEnergies halves buybacks as low oil, gas prices weigh on profits
STORY: French oil giant TotalEnergies will halve share buybacks in the first quarter.The firm said Wednesday (February 11) it will lower its first-quarter buyback to $750 million worth of shares, echoing similar moves by peers.Total had previously kept buybacks at $2 billion per quarter since mid-2022, and repurchased $1.5 billion in shares in the fourth quarter.The announcement came as the energy major also reported a fall in fourth-quarter net income.It was down to $3.8 billion from $4.4 billion a year earlier - below analyst projections.Low oil and gas prices canceled out soaring fourth-quarter profit from refining fuels and proceeds from renewable assets stake sales.Total said it ramped up oil and gas production to compensate for a big drop in both Brent crude and liquefied natural gas prices.However, earnings for the refining and chemicals business surged by 215%, reaching $1 billion.Total has previously said margins at European refineries during the period jumped 231% compared to the previous year.The company's CEO had attributed the increase to U.S. sanctions on Russian providers and an EU import ban on fuels derived from Russian oil.

company.name: Ceres Power Holdings PLC
company.description: Ceres Power Holdings plc engages in the development and commercialization of fuel cell and electrochemical technology in Europe, Asia, and North America. The company offers cell, stack, and factory; power system and power modules for data centers, commercial power, industrial power, and marine applications; and stack array module and electrolyser module for ammonia, refineries, green steel, and eFuels applications. It also provides a solid oxide electrolysis cell (SOEC) technology to produce green hydrogen; and a solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) technology to generate electrical power from various fuel types, including natural gas, biofuels, hydrogen blends, and pure hydrogen. In addition, the company is involved in the provision of overseas license and royalty services; business development and technical support; development of flow battery technologies for energy storage systems; and administration of registered intellectual property. Ceres Power Holdings plc was incorporated in 2004 and is based in Horsham, the United Kingdom.

The Group builds collaborative, supportive relationships with each of its tenants as it believes working in this way helps raise standards of care and helps its tenants build sustainable businesses.
